target: O supracitado relatório encontra-se em anexo.
english: The aforementioned report is attached herein.
tip: 'Supracitado' is formal bureaucratic language – 'aforementioned'.

target: Se bem que ele tem um ponto.
english: Although, he does have a point.
tip: 'Se bem que' takes indicative – it introduces a concession of fact.

target: Aqui é raiz, não tem frescura!
english: We keep it real here, no faking it!
tip: Raiz literally means root. Calling a place or person raiz says it's rootsy and authentic, no frills.

target: Ela é show de bola, faz tudo direitinho.
english: She's awesome, she does everything just right.
tip: Show de bola literally names a dazzling bit of ball play, a football spectacle now used as all-purpose praise for anything great.

target: Se eu tenho tempo, gosto de ler.
english: If I have time, I like to read.
tip: 'Se' + indicative for general truths/habits.

target: Ele é muito pão-duro, nunca paga nada.
english: He's so stingy, he never pays for anything.
tip: Pão-duro is literally hard bread, and it labels a tightwad too stiff to loosen up and spend.

target: Manda a real, você gostou ou não?
english: Tell me straight–did you like it or not?
tip: Manda comes from mandar, which fronts casual speech commands: manda a real (be honest), manda ver (go for it).

target: Estou com a cabeça nas nuvens hoje.
english: I'm daydreaming today.
tip: 'Estar com a cabeça nas nuvens' = to have one's head in the clouds.

target: Partiu praia no fim de semana?
english: Beach trip this weekend?
tip: Partiu is literally departed, past tense, but it works as let's go: Partiu praia means we're off to the beach.

target: Ela deu conta do recado.
english: She got the job done.
tip: Dar conta de means to handle or manage something. Deu conta do recado is she pulled off the errand she was handed.

target: Ela está com a corda toda hoje!
english: She's full of energy today!
tip: The corda is a wind-up spring, so estar com a corda toda means fully wound up, bursting with energy.

target: Tu é ligeirão, hein? Resolveu tudo rapidinho.
english: You're quick, huh? Solved everything fast.
tip: The -ão ending is an augmentative: ligeiro (quick) plus -ão gives ligeirão, a real quick one. It scales up many adjectives.

target: Esse carioca é sangue bom demais!
english: This guy from Rio has such good vibes!
tip: 'Sangue bom' = good person/cool – carioca slang.

target: Ela é a menina dos olhos do pai.
english: She's the apple of her father's eye.
tip: A menina dos olhos is literally the pupil of the eye, the same body-part image English packs into apple of the eye.

target: Cara, essa festa vai ser irada!
english: Dude, this party is going to be awesome!
tip: Cara is literally face, but as a word you address someone with it's Brazil's all-purpose dude.

target: Prezado senhor, venho por meio desta solicitar informações.
english: Dear sir, I am writing to request information.
tip: Highly formal letter opening – 'venho por meio desta' is standard business Portuguese.

target: Tá osso conseguir emprego nessa cidade.
english: It's rough to get a job in this city.
tip: Osso is literally bone, and tá osso means it's tough going, hard as a bone to chew.

target: Pô, que vacilo! Esqueci a carteira em casa.
english: Man, what a blunder! I forgot my wallet at home.
tip: Vacilo comes from vacilar, the cognate of vacillate: a slip of hesitation that turns into a careless blunder.

target: Não fosse a ajuda dos vizinhos, teríamos perdido tudo.
english: Were it not for the neighbors' help, we would have lost everything.
tip: 'Não fosse' = 'were it not for' – inverted conditional without 'se'.

target: Ele está empurrando com a barriga.
english: He's being lazy.
tip: Empurrar com a barriga is literally to push it along with your belly, shoving a task forward instead of actually doing it.

target: Ela está com o pé na jaca.
english: She's getting ahead of herself.
tip: Com o pé na jaca is literally with your foot in the jackfruit, the image for having gone overboard.

target: Ela tem o rei na barriga.
english: She's full of herself.
tip: Ter o rei na barriga is literally to have the king in your belly, as if pregnant with royalty, so it means acting self-important.

target: Vou dar uma mãozinha para você.
english: I'll give you a hand.
tip: Mãozinha adds the diminutive -inha to mão, a little hand. The tiny form softens the offer of help, a very Brazilian touch.

target: Ele está com a corda no pescoço.
english: He's in a tight spot.
tip: Com a corda no pescoço is literally a rope around the neck, and it points to money or debt pressure, not just any tight spot.

target: Ele está com o pé atrás em relação à proposta.
english: He's suspicious of the proposal.
tip: Com o pé atrás is literally with one foot back, poised to step away, so it means being wary or suspicious.

target: Ela deu uma segurada no emprego.
english: She held on tight to her job.
tip: Dar uma plus a verb-ada makes a quick, casual action: uma segurada (a hold), uma olhada (a look), uma parada (a stop).

target: Essa viagem foi tiro e queda.
english: This trip went off without a hitch.
tip: Tiro e queda is literally a shot and a fall: one shot and the target drops, so it means a sure thing that can't fail.

target: Vou dar um jeitinho nisso.
english: I'll find a way to fix this.
tip: 'Dar um jeitinho' = to find a creative solution – a quintessential Brazilian concept.

target: Ele chutou o balde e pediu demissão.
english: He lost it and quit.
tip: Chutou o balde looks like kick the bucket but is a false friend: it means snapping and giving it all up, never dying.

target: Essa história tem muito mais pano pra manga.
english: There's a lot more to this story.
tip: Pano pra manga is literally cloth for a sleeve, plenty of fabric left to work with, so there's much more to the story.
